An interface for [@Document] classes that carry a decision to set a field of the given type in an
 entity. These `Set*Field` classes are used as properties of `Upgrade*Params` classes, always
 nullable. The convention is that when the property is set to `null`, the field of the entity is
 not modified. Otherwise, it is set to the value carried by the `Set*Field` object. In particular,
 for a nullable field, that value could be `null` which allows setting a field of the entity to
 `null`.

description:
Searches for images and videos based on a user's text query.
 This function is designed to parse the user's request for specific details like dates, time ranges, and locations (city and country) to perform a refined search.
 For optimal results, you should extract these details into the corresponding optional fields (startTime, endTime, city, country, countryCode) whenever they are mentioned, in addition to creating a detailed queryString.
FindPhotosResponse The found content's response with media items and resources (MAX = 50)

(Required) Contains only the part of the user's utterance or input relevant to photo search. This should contain only the descriptive part of the user's request that relates to the photos or videos being searched for, including modifiers like location, time, subjects, and other qualifying attributes. Command words like "find", "show", "get" should be excluded, keeping only the content description. Examples: - "photos I took in Paris last year" (from "Find photos I took in Paris last year") - "pictures from my trip to Tokyo in December" (from "Show me pictures from my trip to Tokyo in December") - "videos of my dog playing in the park yesterday" (from "Videos of my dog playing in the park yesterday") - "sunset photos from my vacation in Hawaii" (from "Find sunset photos from my vacation in Hawaii")

description: The ANC mode. The values for this parameter are as follows: - OFF: This mode completely deactivates the Active Noise Cancellation feature. - ON: This mode activates the Active Noise Cancellation feature. - TRANSPARENCY: This mode uses external microphones to intentionally pick up and amplify surrounding sounds, feeding them into the user's ears along with their audio. This allows the user to remain aware of their environment without removing the headphones. It's useful for conversations, hearing announcements, or for safety when outdoors near traffic. - ADAPTIVE: Only available on some new Pixel Buds devices. This mode dynamically adjusts the level of noise reduction and sound transparency based on the user's surrounding environment. It aims to provide a more seamless and intelligent listening experience by automatically balancing noise blocking with environmental awareness.

description: Class for a device state item.

A String uniquely identifying this specific setting that matches with the key in the metadata
 response.

The human-readable name or label for this setting as it appears *exactly* in the Settings UI,
 localized according to `deviceStateLocale`. Example: "Wi-Fi", "Brightness level", "Show
 notifications". Optional: Might not always be available or easily scrapable. Primarily useful
 for display verification or showing back to the user, less critical for LLM logic than the
 `purpose`. Assumes `LocalizedString` handles the actual localized text.

This JSON string serves as a direct pass-through to LLM It is intended only for consumption by
 the LLM, and developers are not expected to parse it manually. This is optional - we don't
 necessarily have the value but we still want to let Gemini know the item exists so it can point
 the user towards the relevant screen
The last time this setting was retrieved real time (not from the cache).

Optional natural language hints or instructions for the LLM on how to interpret the preference
 and its`jsonValue`. This can clarify units, scales, valid ranges, relationships to other
 settings, or constraints. Examples:
 - "Value is a percentage (0-100)."
 - "Enum values: 'ENABLED', 'DISABLED', 'ASK'."
 - "Scale from 0 (off) to 10 (max)."
 - "This setting is only effective if 'master.switch.key' is enabled."
 - "This setting can be changed by the device care app, package name: com.oem.devicecare" Use
   clear, LLM-interpretable language.

Provides details for settings that are duplicated across multiple items. For example,
 notification settings are duplicated for each app.

 Each item in the list represents an "itemization type" (e.g., "package" for per-app or "sim"
 for per-SIM settings). The `key` in [ItemizationType] is the itemization type, and the `values`
 list contains all items of that type on the device.

 For the "package" itemization type, the `values` list would contain an [ItemizationDetail] for
 each app, where `key` is the package name and `value` is the user-friendly app name.

 A [PerScreenMetadata] with a non-empty `itemizationTypes` refers to a generic screen whose
 settings apply to every item in the corresponding list in this field.
